# Structure-Preserving Anonymisation

Redaction destroys the thing being studied. If the finding *is* that many nominally independent
people share one contact address, blacking out the address deletes the finding. Structure-preserving
anonymisation is the alternative: replace every value, keep every relationship.

> "Reconciling those is the whole trick: replace every *value*, preserve every *relationship*."
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/docs/methodology.md, 2026-07-11

## What "preserve every relationship" means concretely

In [[labour-fraud-analysis]] the properties the analysis depends on are enumerated and each is
carried across deliberately:

| Property in the source | Why it must survive | How |
|---|---|---|
| The same person appears in six tables | joins, and the graph | [[deterministic-seeded-substitution]] — same input maps to the same output everywhere |
| A batch of documents has consecutive serial numbers | the bulk-filing signal | the batch is offset by a constant, so contiguity is preserved |
| Many people share one contact point | [[shared-identifier-clustering]] | the sharing is a join key, so it maps identically |
| Identifiers have a recognisable shape | parsers, regexes and the eye | [[format-preserving-invalid-identifiers]] |
| Some dates are wrong, from OCR | the dataset must exercise the same cleaning problems | errors are copied, not fixed |

> "Data-quality artifacts — wrong dates from OCR are preserved so the dataset exercises the same
> cleaning problems as the original."
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/docs/methodology.md, 2026-07-11

Two of these preserved properties are **regression-tested** — the shared-contact concentration and
the bulk-filing batch each have a test asserting the pattern still exists after anonymisation. Testing
that a finding survived the privacy pipeline is the part most implementations skip. See
[[reproducible-analysis]].

## Free text is the hard part

Structured columns are easy: you know which column holds what. Prose does not announce its
identifiers. The pipeline makes three passes — a length-sorted, boundary-aware replacement (with the
word boundary deliberately widened so that an identifier glued to a filename by an underscore is
still caught), a glossary pass that also cleans up orphaned grammatical particles left behind by
substitution, and a residual regex sweep. Each pass exists because the previous one demonstrably
missed something. The [[disclosure-gate]] is what proves the passes worked.

The module that does this holds no source strings in its own text:

> "This script may reference real strings *at run time* because it reads them from the private
> source; it contains none in its own text."
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/src/anonymize.py, 2026-07-11

## Stated limitation — residual source signalling

`docs/methodology.md` §4 claims the world is relocated and that no origin-signalling scrap survives.
**That claim is not fully borne out by the committed code.** Column names retain the source
jurisdiction's identifier registers (`pesel`, `nip`, `regon`, `krs`) and carry through the DDL, the
CSV headers, the dashboard and the generated data dictionary; the validator's allow-list contains the
source country's name and adjective; one PII pattern is a country-specific phone prefix; the viewer
still formats numbers with that jurisdiction's locale; and one generator comment names a
jurisdiction-specific company form.

None of these is a person-like value, and none re-identifies anyone. But **together they narrow both
the host jurisdiction and the worker-origin corridor**, which is exactly the class of inference the
methodology says it removed. Recorded here as a limitation of the implementation, not of the
technique. It is one of the reasons every page for this repo is `publish: false`.
